subject: Bruel et al. (2023)
object: Bruel et al. (2023) described OFDS-RAB34, a new form of oral-facial-digital syndrome caused by biallelic RAB34 variants. Along with oral-facial-digital features, it includes cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.

subject: Bruel et al. (2023)
object: Bruel et al. (2023) reported 4 affected individuals from 3 unrelated families with a new form of oral-facial-digital syndrome. Besides defects of the face, oral cavity and digits, they had cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.

subject: Bruel et al. (2023)
object: In 4 individuals with oral-facial-digital syndrome from 3 unrelated families, Bruel et al. (2023) used exome sequencing to identify biallelic missense variants in the RAB34 gene. The variants clustered near the C terminus of RAB34. The abstract does not give the individual variants.

subject: Bruel et al. (2023)
object: In functional studies, Bruel et al. (2023) found that the mutant RAB34 proteins showed strong loss of function. Some variants could still be recruited to the mother centriole, but cells expressing mutant RAB34 had a significant defect in cilium assembly. RAB34 acts selectively in cell types that use the intracellular ciliogenesis pathway, and the authors concluded that RAB34 is the first small GTPase involved in OFDS.

subject: Batkovskyte et al. (2024)
object: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) reported a fetus with an atypical skeletal ciliopathy phenotype. The fetus had multiple malformations: posterior neck edema, micrognathia, low-set and small ears, auricular hypoplasia, cleft lip and palate, short extremities, and a combination of preaxial and postaxial polydactyly, which rarely occur together.

subject: Batkovskyte et al. (2024)
object: In a fetus with a skeletal ciliopathy phenotype, Batkovskyte et al. (2024) identified compound heterozygous variants in the RAB34 gene by genome sequencing: a maternally inherited missense variant, c.254T>C (p.Ile85Thr), and a paternally inherited nonsense variant, c.691C>T (p.Arg231Ter). Only the paternal variant was present in the unaffected sibling. The authors noted that Rab34-null mice display a ciliopathy phenotype with cleft palate and polydactyly, supporting pathogenicity, and suggested RAB34 as a candidate gene for skeletal ciliopathies.

subject: Batkovskyte et al. (2024)
object: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) cited evidence from the literature that Rab34-null mice display a ciliopathy phenotype with cleft palate and polydactyly, features consistent with those in their patient.
